thread:
jamie: fyi — customer acme-prod reports a sudden p99 regression during their billing-window run (~2:00–2:20 UTC). They're seeing p99 ~7s (was ~600ms) + intermittent 401s. Customer says requests pile up and some fail with attach timeouts. Attaching their partial logs they pasted:

jamie: ```
2026-03-17T02:05:12Z ERROR attach: attach_timeout id=req-8d4f pool=dedicated-eu-west-5
2026-03-17T02:05:12Z WARN  auth: token_validation error uid=acme-prod code=401
2026-03-17T02:05:20Z INFO  scaleup: queue_wait=132s pool=dedicated-eu-west-5
2026-03-17T02:06:00Z ERROR provisioning: coldgpu_init=34s image_pull=21s
```

jamie: they asked us to triage urgently (customer is paying priority).

sophia: can you paste the pool id + tenant + any request ids you have? also which model variant? we need to see if the autoscaler kept failing to attach or if the attach succeeded but model init slow.

jamie: pool=dedicated-eu-west-5, tenant=acme-prod, model=llama-2-13b-8bit, req ids: req-8d4f, req-8d50, req-8d51. they mention auth 401s around the same time as attach timeouts.

lee: I pulled control-plane metrics — there's a clear scaleup-queue backlog spike starting 02:03 UTC. Attach error rate + auth failures coincide. From control-plane logs we see repeated attach handshakes failing:```
[02:04:11] attacher: handshake failed: rpc deadline exceeded (30s)
[02:04:42] attacher: attach timeout reached (90s)
[02:05:18] provisioner: coldgpu init took 34s, kernel setup 12s
```

lee: hypothesis: two simultaneous issues: (1) a burst of auth service latency returning 401s for some tokens causing retries and queue pressure, and (2) image/kernel init jitter on new warmups (cold GPUs) making attach slower — combined they pushed scale-up backlog -> p99 spike.

kai: temporary mitigations to reduce customer impact: 1) increase min-pool for dedicated-eu-west-5 to keep some GPUs warm, 2) route acme-prod critical traffic to hosted fallback (if permitted), 3) bump fairshare for tenant while we investigate.

kai: commands (if we want a quick ramp):
```
# increase min pool to 3 (from 1)
redwoodctl pools update --pool dedicated-eu-west-5 --min 3 --reason "emergency keep-warm for acme-prod p99 spike"
# bump tenant priority
redwoodctl tenants update acme-prod --fairshare-weight 2
```

sophia: agreed. also open an infra ticket to look at kernel image layers — we saw image_pull=21s which is higher than normal. Could be registry flakiness or network congestion in the region. I'll check registry_recent_errors and the node startup traces.

infra-bot: [alert] autoscale: scaleup-latency > 120s for pool dedicated-eu-west-5 between 02:03 and 02:08 UTC. triggered 3 alerts (pager).

jamie: i've told the customer we're investigating and asked for any additional logs. they're ok with a short routing workaround.

lee: SOP for now: sophia will run the min-pool increase and open a kernel/image follow-up. kai will prepare hosted-fallback routing + fairshare bump. jamie will confirm with customer and collect additional request traces for the 401s. i'll keep watching p95/p99 dashboards.

sophia: running pool update now and creating infra ticket (INFRA-2026). will post results in thread.

jamie: thanks — please ping me once hosted fallback is ready so i can coordinate traffic switchover with the customer. :eyes:

kai: prepping the routing change and playbook. if min-pool doesn't help we'll consider temporary canary on hosted models for their tenant. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: ticket INFRA-2026 created: investigate kernel image pull latency in eu-west region.

jamie: noted. owners: sophia (pool + infra ticket), kai (routing + fairshare), lee (monitoring), jamie (customer comms). will follow up in 30m with status. :white_check_mark:
